Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

bayesnec 3.0.0

Breaking changes

Removed functions, methods and arguments

  • average_estimates() is removed. To combine estimates from several fits, call nec(), nsec() or ecx() with posterior = TRUE on each fit and combine the draws (#403).

  • nsec() no longer has methods for brmsfit and drc objects. Use toxval::nsec() for those fits (#555).

  • ecx(), nsec(), compare_estimates() and compare_posterior() no longer take hormesis_def. Every ECx and NSEC is measured from the control, which is what the default hormesis_def = "control" selected. ecx(), nsec(), nec(), ecnsec() and compare_posterior() stop with an error that names the argument, and compare_estimates() with “unused argument”; remove it from the call. Nothing replaces hormesis_def = "max". Its removal changes the position of the arguments after it in ecx(), nsec() and compare_estimates(), so a call that passes them by position must name them (#195).

Changed defaults

  • nec(), nsec(), ecx(), curve_params(), exceedance(), ggbnec_data(), plot() and autoplot() default to xform = NULL, and summary() reports on the same scale. Where crf() transforms the predictor inline, as in crf(log(concentration)), an estimate is returned on the scale the predictor was recorded on, a concentration, where 2.1.3.1 returned it on the transformed scale. compare_estimates() and compare_posterior() compare on the same scale. Calls that pass xform = exp return estimates on the scale they did before. xform = identity is equivalent to the default for each estimator. Write x_scale = "fitted" to return the transformed scale; the estimators and plotting methods use the same argument. A fit whose predictor is an untransformed column is unaffected. See ?nec (#299).

  • The default resolution of ecx() and nsec() is 500 instead of 1000, and that of compare_estimates() 500 instead of 100. ecx() and nsec() interpolate between grid points to find the concentration at which the curve crosses the target. The grid bnec() stores with a fit is unchanged (#325, #527, #578).

  • bnec() fits on the identity link unless the call writes a link or passes a family object held in a variable, which keeps its links. A family object such as Beta(), Gamma(), binomial() or poisson() kept the link of its constructor in 2.1.3.1 (logit, inverse, logit, log), and now fits on the identity link, so estimates and default priors change. Write Beta(link = "logit") to keep the earlier model. update() applies the same rules to a supplied family. See the link section of ?bnec (#256).

  • rhat() uses a cutoff of 1.01 instead of 1.05 and ignores the prior_* draws (#148).

  • compare_estimates(), compare_fitted(), compare_posterior() and sample_priors() gain seed, 10 by default, and leave the session’s random number stream unchanged, so a preceding set.seed() no longer changes their results. compare_estimates() and compare_fitted() pair a random subset of the longer posterior rather than its first draws. Results differ from 2.1.3.1 (#218, #343).

  • amend(), update(), pull_out() and c() reuse the x_range, resolution, sig_val and loo_controls a model set was fitted with, where 2.1.3.1 reset them to the defaults. An equation added by amend() takes the set’s prior, prior_type, asymptote_observed, predictor_scale, control and seed. A set fitted by 2.1.3.1 records none of these settings, so the defaults still apply to it (#489, #522).

Changed estimates for the same call

  • For a posterior draw whose curve does not reach the target within the prediction range, nsec() and ecx() no longer return the grid point nearest the target, and nec() no longer reports a sampled nec beyond that range as a value. Such a draw is censored instead. A summary quantile that falls among censored draws is reported as the bound, summary() and the plot annotations mark it >= or <=, and a warning gives the number of draws affected. Once any draw is censored, the quantiles are order statistics of the draws. With posterior = TRUE, a draw censored above the search range is Inf and one censored below it is -Inf, and a curve-read draw stored in a fit’s ne_posterior or w_ne_posterior takes the same form. The attr(, "censored") record retains the bounds and affected draws. These infinite values keep their positions in sort() and quantile(). A posterior with no censored draw is summarised as before. See ?nec (#39, #395).

  • ecx() and nsec() measure every estimate from the control, the predicted mean at the lowest observed concentration or at the x_control given to bnec(), and take the first concentration at or above the control where a draw’s curve crosses the target. 2.1.3.1 measured type = "absolute" from the highest point of the curve, read the control at the first point of the prediction grid, so that x_range changed it, and took the grid point nearest the target anywhere in the range. An NSEC draw already past the reference at the control takes a later decreasing crossing where there is one; otherwise it takes the control concentration, or is censored above the range where the curve later rises above the reference (#195, #527, #586, #589).

  • ecx(type = "relative") measures from the control to the equation’s lower asymptote, bot, taken on the response scale under a log or logit link, and warns that its meaning has changed. For an equation without bot it measures towards 0, the value the mean declines to under each link. The quantity 2.1.3.1 reported, from the top of the fitted curve to its lowest point, is now type = "range", measured from the control. type = "relative" is an error for an equation without bot on a family unbounded below, such as nec3param on a gaussian response. The same applies to compare_estimates() and compare_posterior() (#195, #578).

  • The ecnsec_relativeP attribute of nsec() is the percent effect at each draw’s own NSEC measured from the control, and equals ecnsec() under type = "absolute". The effect is zero where the NSEC is the control concentration. It is negative where a draw’s control is below the reference and its NSEC is a later crossing, because its response there exceeds its own control (#195, #605).

  • nec(), summary() and the plots report the NSEC as the no-effect estimate of the six hormesis threshold equations, nechorme, nechorme4, neclinhorme, nechormepwr, nechorme4pwr and nechormepwr01, where 2.1.3.1 reported their nec parameter. That parameter is the concentration at which the decline term starts, where the response can still be above the control, and curve_params() returns it. The model-averaged N(S)EC changes wherever these equations contribute. nec() still returns the sampled nec of nec3param, nec4param, neclin and necsigm (#570).

  • For a group-level term whose levels span concentrations, nec(), nsec() and ecx() read the curve of each observed level, with its fitted deviation, and by default pool the levels as an observation-weighted mixture. 2.1.3.1 read the population curve, with the deviations at zero. See “Estimates from observed group levels” below (#554, #557).

  • The default nec and ec50 prior is a lognormal centred on the median of the log of the distinct positive concentrations, or a normal for a predictor already on the log scale, so replicates no longer shift it. It is still bounded to the tested range (#269, #302, #314, #483).

  • The default top and bot priors for a poisson or negbinomial response that contains zeros are scaled from its positive values (#210, #232).

  • bnec() sets default priors on group-level standard deviations and on the ogl() intercept, which 2.1.3.1 left at the brms defaults (#245, #257).

  • The initial-value search accepts each chain separately, checks the curve against a band built from the level means, and re-draws a single parameter when a full draw fails. It rejects a draw at which an exp() in the curve would overflow, keeps refined values inside the prior bounds, and stops with an error after a set number of redraws. A fit with the same seed therefore starts from other initial values than under 2.1.3.1 (#162, #266, #309, #578).

  • bnec() no longer replaces a zero in the predictor with a tenth of the smallest positive value. The control is fitted at 0, which changes the estimates of such fits (#269).

  • The default model set and the "ecx" and "decline" groups include ecxflat, a new equation whose mean is constant, so model weights and model-averaged estimates change (#419, #485).

  • A gaussian model set keeps the equations of the zero_bounded group, which 2.1.3.1 excluded, so a default gaussian fit includes eleven more equations (#206).

  • On the identity link, nechormepwr and nechorme4pwr are excluded for bernoulli, binomial, beta_binomial and Beta responses, and ecxhormebc5 for a predictor with negative values on a family whose mean cannot be negative (#177, #344).

  • Where each level of a group-level term is observed at a single concentration, such as ogl(conc_group) on lum31, model weights are computed by leaving out each level whole rather than each observation. loo_controls = list(leave_out = "observation") restores the earlier score (#529, #531).

  • Model-averaged estimates and predictions are drawn once when a model set is built and recorded in w_draw_index, so fitted(), posterior_epred(), ecx() and nsec() give the same result on every call (#216).

  • bnec() fits an equation with a group-level term at adapt_delta = 0.99 where the family bounds the mean and that term could take it outside the bound. A value supplied in control takes precedence (#257, #294).

  • Group-level deviations on a family whose mean is bounded, fitted on the identity link, are applied multiplicatively: on the odds for Beta, binomial, bernoulli and beta_binomial, and on the value for Gamma, poisson and negbinomial. This applies to an ogl() deviation, for the equations whose curve stays inside the bounds of the family, and to a pgl(), (top | g) or (bot | g) term on top or bot. The standard deviation of a term on top or bot is then reported as sd(topgl_Intercept) or sd(botgl_Intercept), on the log or log-odds scale, so code that reads those draws by name must use the new names. See ?bayesnecformula (#257, #294).

  • A user prior that omits a parameter is completed from the default priors, with a warning naming each parameter filled, rather than leaving it on the flat prior of brms (#207).

  • bnec() and bnec_group() fit ecxflat alone, with a message, to a bernoulli, binomial, beta_binomial or Beta response at one bound in every observation (#400, #419, #441).

  • manec_example is refitted under this release from data-raw/manec_example.R, with two chains of 1200 post-warmup draws and seed 10, where the 2.1.3.1 object held two chains of 50. Both equations pass screen_models() at its defaults, bnec_version() returns the installation that fitted it, and the object no longer stores the compiled Stan model. Values computed from it differ from those of the 2.1.3.1 object (#579).

Corrected results

The defects of 2.1.3.1 below are corrected, and each correction changes what the same call returns.

  • ogl() and pgl() fit a/b, a:b, a*b and a gr() grouping as written, rather than as separate terms on each variable they name. A gr() grouping with by, such as pgl(gr(plate, by = toxicant)), fits one standard deviation for each level of by. A gr() grouping in a (par | group) term is refused with a message naming the pgl() and ogl() form (#466, #550).

  • bnec() keeps a boundary shift of the response where crf() transforms the predictor, and refuses a transformed response that sits on a boundary (#258).

  • bnec() uses the intended number of trials where trials() contains arithmetic; 2.1.3.1 applied it twice.

  • ecx(), nsec() and the stored NSEC apply arithmetic inside an inline transformation, such as crf(log(x + 1)), to the estimate correctly (#196).

  • amend(), c() and + recompute the LOO and WAIC criteria of every equation, so the weights of a combined set come from the same settings (#522).

  • The sample_size of a model set counts the draws each equation holds where thin does not divide the post-warmup iterations (#477).

  • fitted(), predict(), posterior_epred() and posterior_predict() on a model set return one row for a one-row newdata, where 2.1.3.1 returned one for each point of the stored grid, with a warning.

  • summary(ecx = TRUE) reads each ECx over the fit’s prediction range and passes x_range, resolution and xform to ecx() (#395, #439).

  • dispersion() uses the link the model was fitted with, rather than the family’s default link, so its value changes for a poisson or binomial fit on the identity link. It returns a value where a fitted variance is zero, and leaves the session’s random number stream where it was (#247, #298, #337).

  • models() given a numeric range returns the equations bnec() fits for that range: all 24 for c(-Inf, Inf), where 2.1.3.1 returned 12 (#170).

  • plot() and autoplot() draw the NEC and EC10 annotations at the matching point of the curve where the predictor is transformed, apply xform to the predictor axis whenever the predictor itself is untransformed, and order the interval correctly under a decreasing xform (#160, #161, #268, #417).

  • plot() and autoplot() annotate the same EC10 on a gaussian fit, measured with type = "range". 2.1.3.1 annotated a relative ECx in plot() and an absolute one in autoplot().

  • c(), + and update() weight a model set by pseudo-BMA, as bnec() does; 2.1.3.1 used stacking (#320).

Changed return values

  • A fitted object no longer contains pred_vals$posterior, and a model set no longer contains w_pred_vals$posterior. Obtain the matrix with posterior_epred(fit, newdata = bnec_newdata(fit, resolution = 1000), re_formula = NA). Objects saved by 2.1.3.1 keep it (#180, #213).

  • compare_estimates() and compare_posterior() compare a censored draw through its censored attribute. prob_diff gains prob_lower, prob_upper, censored_first and censored_second, and diff_data gains positive and indeterminate. prob is NA where censoring leaves the order of some pairs undetermined, so code reading prob must handle NA (#404).

  • dispersion(summary = TRUE) returns a fourth element, P(>1), the posterior probability of over-dispersion (#262).

  • The "toxicity_estimate" attribute of a nec() result is "nec" where every draw is a sampled NEC, "nsec" where every draw is an NSEC, and "n(s)ec" where a model set or a hurdle fit combines the two. 2.1.3.1 set it to "nec" whatever the equation (#570).

Newly refused input

  • bnec() refuses a brms additional-response term other than trials(), weights(), cens() and rate(). 2.1.3.1 passed such a term on after a message. Remove the term, or fit the model with brms::brm() (#136).

  • bnec() refuses a crf() predictor written with a formula operator at its top level, such as crf(-x), crf(x - 1) or crf(x^2). 2.1.3.1 fitted such a model on x alone while ecx() and nsec() applied the expression to the estimate, so the reported values were wrong. Write crf(I(x - 1)) or compute a column. ecx(), nsec() and autoplot() refuse an earlier fit with such a predictor (#438, #479).

  • bnec(), bnec_group(), bnec_hurdle(), get_priors() and update() refuse a missing value in any variable the formula names, and report the rows. Apply na.omit() to the data first. 2.1.3.1 stopped with an unrelated error on a bare column and, under an inline transformation, fitted the complete rows (#278).

  • bnec() refuses a link other than identity, log or logit (#256).

  • bnec() refuses a data column named bnecmu, ogl, topgl, bnectop, botgl or bnecbot, and a user prior on top or bot without the bounds of the family where a group-level term applies to it (#257, #294).

  • bnec() and amend() refuse, before fitting, a prior that is not a brmsprior or a named list of them with unique names. 2.1.3.1 replaced such a prior with the defaults without a message (#543, #552).

  • bnec(), bnec_group(), amend() and update() check the data once before fitting. They refuse a value of the predictor or response that is not finite, a rate() denominator of zero or less, a predictor with a single value and data with no rows, and under binomial or beta_binomial trials that are not a positive whole number or are fewer than the response. bnec_group() refuses a level observed at a single concentration, and warns of one observed at two (#578).

  • bnec(), bnec_group(), amend() and update() refuse, before fitting, a sig_val outside (0, 1), a resolution that is not a whole number of at least 2, an x_range that is not NA or an increasing pair, and an equation name that is not one of the 24. x_var, y_var, trials_var, model, random and random_vars, removed in 2.0, are refused where 2.1.3.1 ignored them with a warning, and so is a second crf() term, which 2.1.3.1 ignored. A crf() term without an equation is refused (#211, #325, #578).

  • nsec() refuses a sig_val outside (0, 1). ecx(), nsec() and ecnsec() refuse a resolution that is not a whole number of at least 2, ecx() refuses a missing or vector ecx_val, and all four estimators refuse a posterior that is not TRUE or FALSE. nsec() refuses type and any other argument it does not use, which 2.1.3.1 ignored. nec() says that it does not use sig_val, resolution or x_range, and its refusal of a smooth equation points to nsec(). bnec_newdata() refuses a resolution that is not a whole number (#578).

  • compare_posterior() refuses an argument in ... except under comparison = "fitted", which 2.1.3.1 ignored. compare_estimates(), compare_posterior() and compare_fitted() refuse a single fit or a list of fewer than two fits. compare_estimates() and compare_posterior() refuse an unknown comparison and a NEC comparison of a smooth equation, and compare_fitted() an ndraws or draw_ids outside the draws (#578).

  • pull_out() refuses an argument in ..., which 2.1.3.1 ignored (#578).

  • bnec() refuses a name in loo_controls$weights that the weighting method does not read, which 2.1.3.1 ignored (#578, #583).

  • bnec() refuses a poisson or negbinomial response with no positive value, and a Beta response of 0 in every observation (#210, #232, #400).

  • autoplot() and ggbnec_data() refuse dpar, and a which they cannot draw. 2.1.3.1 ignored both, or stopped with “unused argument” under ecx = TRUE (#564, #565).

  • c() refuses to combine a fit from 2.1.3.1 whose zero predictor was replaced with a new fit of the same data; refit it (#269).

Dependencies

  • bayesnec requires brms 2.23.0 or later, and no longer imports evaluate (#249, #578).

Grouped fits

  • bnec_group() fits a model set separately at each level of a factor and returns a bayesnecgroupfit. Its nec(), nsec(), ecx(), ecnsec(), exceedance() and curve_params() methods return one row for each level, with bound_ columns marking censored entries, and take pool to combine the levels. It also has print(), summary(), plot(), autoplot(), ggbnec_data(), amend(), compare_posterior() and failed_models() methods, and dispersion() refuses it in favour of a call on each level. bnec_newdata(), fitted(), predict(), posterior_epred(), posterior_predict(), pp_check(), rhat(), check_chains(), check_priors(), pull_brmsfit(), pull_best(), get_priors(), formula() and model.frame() accept a checked level argument. Without it, matrices, plots, priors and brms fits are named by level; tables with matching columns include a level column. update() refits every level, while c() and + combine matching grouped fits within each level. check_sampling(), group_level_sd() and pull_prior() also report results by level. With family = NULL the family is chosen once from the whole response. A numeric grouping column, fewer than two levels, or a level with fewer than four observations is refused before fitting. Each level’s seed is derived from a seed passed through ..., or else from the session’s random number stream, and is stored in level_seeds. Under a future plan the levels or the equations take the workers, whichever needs fewer rounds. See ?bnec_group and the article Grouping and factor covariates (#33, #338, #557).

  • check_fit() on a bayesnecgroupfit checks each level and returns a checkfit_group object, with print() and plot() methods (#562, #563).

  • nec() and exceedance() on a bayesnecgroupfit return NA for a level fitted with a single smooth equation, which has no nec parameter, and say so in one message that names the level and points to nsec(), as they do for a bayesnecjointfit. Where every level is of that kind they stop. A level holding a model set returns its model-averaged N(S)EC.

  • crossed_group_weights() gives the model weights of each level of a bayesnecgroupfit, the best combination of per-level equations with its weight, and the weights of the equations common to every level. Given a pooled fit, it compares the grouped and pooled fits on the leave-one-group-out score, as LOOIC, where that score was computed for every fit over the same levels, and on WAIC otherwise. It refuses a set weighted by stacking (#33, #531).

  • compare_posterior() accepts a bayesnecgroupfit, whose levels it compares, as well as a named list of fits (#33).

  • group_level_sd() tabulates the group-level standard deviations of each equation, such as those of an ogl() or pgl() term, beside the equation’s model weight. It accepts a bayesnecfit, a bayesmanecfit, a bayesnecgroupfit, with a level column, and a bayesnechurdlefit, with one table per component (#532).

  • ggbnec_data() gains group, and autoplot() gains group and group_aes, which joins the means of each level of a grouping variable or colours its observations (#368).

Estimates from observed group levels

  • For a group-level term whose levels span concentrations, nec(), nsec(), ecx() and ecnsec() read the curve of each observed level, including its fitted deviation. A level observed at only one concentration is excluded, with a message naming it. This applies to single fits, model sets, hurdle fits and joint refits, and to the no-effect estimate stored at fitting (#554, #557).

  • pool chooses how the levels are combined: "none" returns per-level estimates, "mixture" gives each posterior draw to one level in proportion to its observation count, "mean_estimate" averages the levels’ estimates at each draw, and "mean_curve" estimates from their weighted mean curve. A joint refit and a grouped fit default to "none", and a single fit, model set or hurdle fit with a spanning group term to "mixture". nec() refuses "mean_curve". x_control = "own", the default, reads each level from the control recorded at fitting, or else from its lowest observed concentration, "shared" reads every level from the lowest control, and a number gives the control concentration, with a warning where it extrapolates a level’s curve and a message where it replaces the lower end of x_range (#557, #578).

  • The curve and credible band of autoplot() and ggbnec_data() remain the population curve, with the group deviations at zero, so the estimate lines need not fall where that curve equals the corresponding response (#576).

Hurdle and zero-inflated models

  • bnec() accepts the two-block families hurdle_gamma, zero_inflated_beta, hurdle_poisson and hurdle_negbinomial, and the single-block families zero_inflated_poisson and zero_inflated_negbinomial. A two-block family fits one curve to the positive response, on the untruncated mean for a count hurdle, and a second, the zero block, to the probability of a non-zero response, while a single-block family holds that probability constant. Each family must be named in family; bnec() never chooses one. The new model_survival argument names the equation for the zero block. The zero block is fitted on the identity link, and another link for it is refused. neclin, neclinhorme, ecxlin, nechormepwr and nechorme4pwr are excluded for every two-block family, and nechormepwr01 as well where the positive block is a Gamma or count response on the identity link. For a two-block family posterior_epred() returns the mean of the positive block multiplied by the probability of a non-zero response. A zero_inflated_beta response at one bound in every observation is treated as a Beta response is (#104, #173, #209, #249).

  • ecx() and nsec() gain dpar, which reports one block of a joint two-block fit. Under dpar = "mu" a count hurdle reports the mean of the positive counts. On a two-block fit ecx(type = "relative") without dpar is refused, and so is ecnsec(type = "relative") (#249, #491).

  • autoplot() and ggbnec_data() on a two-block fit take which. which = "all" draws the combined curve, the response of survivors and the probability of survival in three panels, each with the no-effect estimate and ECx of its own block, the NSEC for a hormesis threshold equation, and titled with the equation of each block it reads; "growth" or "survival" draws one of them. ggbnec_data() returns a panel column naming the curve of each row (#564, #565).

  • bnec_hurdle() fits a hurdle model as two bnec() fits: the growth of the units with a non-zero response, and a bernoulli model for survival. It returns a bayesnechurdlefit, whose estimators, plots and predictions take which = "combined", "growth" or "survival". The combined NEC is the per-draw minimum of the two components. formula() returns the growth and survival formulas. Prediction methods pass draw selection and newdata to both components. A disp() term applies to the growth component, and so does a cens() term where the growth family is continuous. trials() and weights() are refused, as are binomial, beta_binomial, zero-inflated count and two-block growth families. crossed_weights() gives the weight of every growth and survival pair, and best_crossed() names the highest. autoplot() marks each panel’s no-effect estimate and its credible limits, and the ECx when ecx = TRUE, and plot() labels each estimate NEC, NSEC or N(S)EC. Its ggbnec_data() and autoplot() refuse add_nec and add_ecx. See ?bnec_hurdle and the article Hurdle and zero-inflated concentration-response models (#188, #249, #412, #415, #547).

  • bnec_hurdle() fits count survivors, with a poisson or negbinomial growth family, by a zero-truncated likelihood, which needs brms 2.23.2 or later. With an earlier brms it stops before fitting and names the joint count hurdle, bnec(family = "hurdle_poisson") or bnec(family = "hurdle_negbinomial"), which brms 2.23.0 fits (#249).

Joint refits

  • bnec_joint() refits a factorised fit as one model. For a bayesnechurdlefit it refits the pair best_crossed() names with the matching two-block family. For a bayesnecgroupfit it composes the equation each level favours into one model in which every curve parameter takes a value per level, and returns a bayesnecjointfit. With disp_by_level = TRUE, the default, the dispersion parameter also takes a value per level. Each level is read over its own concentrations, from the control recorded at fitting or given as bnec_joint(x_control = ), or else from its lowest concentration. prior_type, asymptote_observed and predictor_scale are taken from the fit unless supplied, and an argument that applies only to the other kind of fit is refused. See ?bnec_joint and the article Grouping and factor covariates (#382, #388, #448, #500, #516, #557, #578).

  • A bayesnecjointfit has explicit methods for its shared posterior, and a method that returns one result per fit returns one per level. Its internal level adapter exposes the four toxicity estimators without inheriting the ordinary-fit prediction and diagnostic methods. summary() gives each level’s no-effect estimate, labelled NEC or NSEC, its ECx values and the Bayesian R-squared of its rows. plot(), pp_check(), check_chains() and check_priors() draw one panel or page per level. rhat(), check_fit(), check_sampling(), curve_params(), dispersion(), formula() and model.frame() return one element, row or table per level, and screen_models() passes or stops the refit as a whole. fitted(), predict(), posterior_epred() and posterior_predict() predict the fitted rows of every level, or a newdata naming one level’s rows. These methods, and those that return one result per level, refuse a level argument, because all levels share one posterior. group_level_sd() reads the refit as one fit. update() refits the same model, get_priors() returns its priors, pull_prior() returns its full prior table, and pull_best() returns it unchanged. amend(), pull_out(), c() and + refuse it, because each of its levels has one equation and it is not a model set (#578).

  • Where a factorised Gamma growth fit includes a left-censored survivor, bnec_joint() fits that row as an interval from zero to the recorded bound, so that the joint likelihood conditions on known survival. A zero_inflated_beta joint refit with such a row is refused (#544, #546).

  • compare_posterior() on a bayesnecjointfit contrasts its levels at the same posterior draw, for the NEC, N(S)EC, NSEC, ECx and fitted curve, so that each contrast keeps the dependence between levels estimated in one posterior. A group term the levels share, such as a batch in which both were tested, is read at the same value for every level at each draw. Separate fits are paired at random (#571, #574).

  • nec() on a bayesnecjointfit names each level’s equation in a model column and the kind of its estimate in an ne_type column. It gives the NEC of a level fitted with a monotone threshold equation, the NSEC of a hormesis threshold equation, and NA, with a message, for a smooth equation. nec(no_effect = TRUE) gives the NSEC of a smooth level as well. Where every level has a smooth equation, nec() stops, as it does for a single smooth equation. The other classes refuse no_effect (#388, #570).

Estimates beyond the prediction range

  • nec(), nsec(), ecx() and ecnsec() gain extrapolate, which widens the bound at which a draw is censored. A finite limit appends points beyond the prediction grid at its spacing, so an estimate found inside the range is unchanged by a limit beyond it, and a limit inside the range is refused. nec(extrapolate = TRUE) removes the bound only where every equation samples its NEC, and is refused for a fit or set that includes a smooth or hormesis threshold equation; the other three refuse TRUE. The default nec prior is bounded to the tested range, so a sampled NEC above it needs asymptote_observed = FALSE. See ?nec (#392, #570, #589).

  • exceedance() gives the posterior probability that a NEC, NSEC or ECx lies above a threshold concentration, such as a guideline value. Censored draws are counted from their censored attribute, and the probability is reported with the lower and upper limits they allow (#44).

Diagnostics

  • check_fit() compares the observed location and spread of the response at each predictor value against the values the fit simulates, and gives a posterior predictive p-value for each comparison, counting ties as one half. Predictor values without replicates are binned, with a warning. Where the observed statistic and the median simulated one are both zero their ratio is reported as 1. A group with one observation gets the mean statistics only. In a group with readings censored through cens(), the observed and simulated values beyond the bound are set to it, and n_cens gives the number censored. It accepts a bayesnecfit, bayesmanecfit, bayesnecgroupfit or bayesnechurdlefit, prints the Pareto k summary of the stored LOO criterion separately, and returns it in the "pareto" attribute. A group argument with missing values or of the wrong length is refused. It has print() and plot() methods (#56, #148, #542, #558, #566, #568, #578).

  • pp_check() has methods for bayesnecfit, bayesmanecfit and bayesnechurdlefit objects. A model set returns one plot per equation (#56, #148).

  • check_sampling() reports the largest Rhat, the smallest effective sample size and the number and proportion of divergent transitions of each equation, and screen_models() drops the equations that fail and reports why. An equation fails on divergences where more than divergence_cutoff of its retained draws are divergent, by default 0.00125 (0.125%), which is 10 of the 8,000 draws bnec() retains by default. Because the cutoff is a proportion, thinning or a longer run at the same rate of divergence does not change, in expectation, the quantity it is compared with (#148, #597).

  • summary() of a single fit or a model set reports the number of divergent transitions of each equation, and its printed output warns where they exceed the new divergence_cutoff, the proportion of retained draws that check_sampling() uses (#447, #597).

  • bnec() reports an equation that does not reproduce the mean or spread of the control. summary() of a model set does the same by default, which simulates from each equation, controlled by the new check_fit and fit_ratio_cutoff arguments (#148).

  • nec(), the printed summary() and curve_params() report a sampled nec or ec50 posterior with more than 7.5 per cent of its draws within the outer 5 per cent of its prior range, where the prior bound may set the credible limit. nec() and summary() give a note and a prior_bound_summary attribute; for a model set it gives each equation’s share and the model-weighted share. The estimates are unchanged (#584).

  • failed_models() returns each equation that bnec() or amend() could not fit, with its error, priors and initial values, and summary() lists them (#133).

Model weights

  • kfold_groups() computes exact K-fold scores over the levels of a grouping, for a single equation or each equation of a model set. Each equation is refitted once without each fold of levels, and each held-out level is scored from that refit with its own deviations integrated out. The levels are assigned to folds within each concentration, or by the caller, and the assignment is stored with the scores. A fold can be computed in its own R process, and kfold_combine() joins the folds. The scores compare with loo::loo_compare(). kfold_weights() weights a model set by them and records loo_controls$leave_out = "kfold", so that amend(), pull_out() and c() keep them (#598).

  • loo_controls takes three new elements. leave_out is "group", the default, "observation" or "kfold". "group" leaves out each level of a group-level term whole where every level is observed at a single concentration, integrating out up to two independent normal intercepts per level, such as an ogl() term together with a (par | group) term. Otherwise each observation is scored, with a warning where such a term exists but cannot be left out. refit = TRUE refits each equation without each level whose Pareto k is at or above 0.7 and scores that level from the refit, and a message says when it has no effect. report_k = FALSE silences the Pareto k report. pull_out() says when it ignores leave_out or refit (#529, #531, #536, #578, #598).

  • When a model set is built, a message gives the number of Pareto k values at or above 0.7 among the scores behind its weights, for each equation with at least 0.01 of the model weight. A second message gives the values below 0.7 that exceed the threshold loo sets for the number of draws (#536, #553).

  • mod_stats gains elpd, the score the weights were computed from, and summary() prints what the score left out. A set fitted by 2.1.3.1 keeps its score when amend(), pull_out(), c() or update() rebuilds it; amend(x, loo_controls = list(leave_out = "group")) recomputes its weights (#531).

Priors

  • bnec() and amend() gain prior_type. prior_type = "regularizing" narrows the default top, bot, nec, ec50 and group-level priors of the default "uninformative", centring top on the response at the lowest concentrations and bot on the response at the highest, and places normal(0, 1) on the curve-shape exponents d and f. beta and slope keep normal(0, 5) under both. See ?bnec and vignette("example3") (#535, #537).

  • bnec() and amend() gain asymptote_observed. FALSE declares that the highest concentration did not reach the lower asymptote. It places the bot prior between the floor of the response and the mean response at the end of the series, removes the upper bound of the nec and ec50 priors, and extends the initial-value search to the floor. For an equation that estimates bot on its default prior, it is refused where the response has no floor, as for a gaussian response with a negative value or a log or logit link, unless prior supplies bot. bnec() reports, before fitting, a response still declining between the two highest concentrations, with the highest mean as a percentage of the control mean. Where that is at most 5 per cent, the report omits the advice to declare the asymptote unobserved. Grouped levels and hurdle blocks are assessed separately (#390, #394, #449, #483, #516, #561, #585).

  • bnec() and amend() gain predictor_scale, "concentration" or "log", which declares the scale of the predictor for the default nec and ec50 priors. The default "auto" treats a predictor with a negative value as logged, and "concentration" refuses a negative predictor (#317).

  • get_priors() returns priors in the form bnec(prior = ) accepts, from a fit or from a formula and data before anything is fitted. It refuses a grouped or joint fit and an argument it does not use (#141, #578).

  • bnec() takes prior as a named argument, and accepts a prior on the family’s dispersion parameter (sigma, shape or phi) (#207).

Dispersion

  • bnec() accepts a disp() term in the formula. disp(~x) models the dispersion parameter on the predictor, and disp("power"), disp("twosided") and disp("loglinear") model it as a function of the mean. It is refused for a family with no free dispersion parameter and for hurdle_poisson and the zero-inflated count families, and a function of the mean is refused under a link other than the identity, as is a disp(~x) term whose values are not finite. On hurdle_gamma, zero_inflated_beta and hurdle_negbinomial it models the positive block. See ?bnec and the article A complete analysis workflow (#191, #397, #410, #443, #468, #472).

  • dispersion() accepts a model set, returning a named list of draws, or with summary = TRUE one row per equation, and a bayesnechurdlefit, for which it returns the growth and survival components. mod_stats gains dispersion_P_over_1, which the weights table of summary() shows where the test applies (#262).

Families, formulas and equations

  • bnec() accepts a rate() term for poisson and negbinomial responses. The curve, its estimates and the plots, observations included, are then per unit of exposure, and the default top and bot priors are built on that scale. The denominator must be a column of the data (#136, #389).

  • bnec() accepts a cens() term. A censored observation keeps its recorded value rather than being shifted off a boundary, and censoring at a bound the family excludes is refused. See vignette("example1") (#181).

  • ecxflat is a new equation whose mean is constant over the predictor. It has no nec parameter, so its no-effect estimate is an NSEC, and every ECx it gives is censored above the prediction range (#419).

  • bayesnecformula() and bnf() gain env, the environment in which a formula given as a string is resolved (#319).

  • models() gains max_pars, the largest number of curve parameters an equation may have (#301).

  • make_brmsformula() gains family, which a two-block family and a disp() term need.

Other new features

  • predict(), plot() and autoplot() on a model set gain model, which names equations to show alongside or instead of the model average, and average. predict() then returns a list. all_models is deprecated and gives a warning whenever it is supplied; all_models = TRUE still works in plot() and autoplot(), and is written model = fit$success_models, average = FALSE (#120).

  • bnec() gains x_control, a stated control concentration, given on the scale the predictor was recorded on. It sets the concentration at which the estimators read the control, the lower bound of the default nec and ec50 priors, the start of the prediction grid, the stored NSEC and the control of the fit checks. Without it the control is the lowest observed concentration. A value that is not a single finite number, a negative value where the predictor is a concentration, a value at or above the highest observed concentration, or one that differs from the lower end of x_range is refused. A control below the lowest concentration tested is reported as an extrapolation, and under prior_type = "regularizing" a control with no observation needs a supplied top prior. bnec_group() and bnec_hurdle() apply it to every level or component, bnec_joint() takes the recorded control unless given its own, amend() and update() reuse it, and c() refuses fits with different controls (#586).

  • ggbnec_data() and autoplot() accept x_scale = "fitted" where crf() transforms the predictor inline. The curve and observations are then drawn on the fitted scale, and the axis is labelled in recorded concentrations, including the ends of the range and a zero control where the transformation is finite at zero. It is refused with an xform other than the identity (#547).

  • autoplot() gains point_alpha, the opacity of the observation points, and every autoplot() method takes xlab and ylab (#533, #565).

  • bnec_record() reports the equations requested, those attempted, those excluded with the reason, and any change made to the response before fitting (#93, #261).

  • bnec_version() reports the bayesnec version, its source and commit, and the R, brms and Stan interface versions that fitted each equation of an object. For an object fitted earlier the source is "unknown" (#464).

  • pull_best() returns the equation of a model set with the most model weight as a bayesnecfit (#324).

  • curve_params() reports the curve parameters of each equation with their credible intervals and model weight (#297).

  • ecnsec() returns the percent effect at each posterior draw’s own NSEC. It takes sig_val to select the control reference and no longer takes nsec, xform or x_scale. For type = "range", draws whose NSEC is above the prediction range have a censored effect (#195, #605).

  • amend() has a method for bayesnecfit. Adding an equation returns a model set (#176).

  • bnec() and amend() fit the equations of a model set in parallel under the future plan in force. Without a plan they are fitted in sequence, as before (#184, #216).

  • bnec() and amend() gain timeout, a time limit for each equation. An equation of a set that exceeds it is recorded as failed, and a single equation stops with an error. A finite limit needs the R.utils package, whose absence is reported before any equation is fitted (#157, #578).

  • New datasets: alga, coral_colour, coral_pam, lum31 and nassarius (#6, #33, #173, #181, #301).

Other changes

  • summary() of a model set flags an equation whose Rhat exceeds the new rhat_cutoff argument, 1.01 by default (#148).

  • pull_out() gains x_range, resolution and sig_val (#489).

  • The initial-value search says so when it is still running after 20 seconds (#309).

  • bnec() reports, once per call, each value of the response it shifts off a boundary of the family (#93).

  • bnec() reports a response that appears normalised to the control or to its maximum (#173).

  • A fit no longer stores the environment its formula was written in, only the objects the formula uses that the data do not supply, so saved fits are smaller (#329).

  • ecx() accepts any ecx_val above 0, and an absolute ECx of a gaussian equation without bot, both of which 2.1.3.1 refused (#206, #325).

  • ggbnec_data() reads the credible band of a single fit from its stored pred_vals rather than from brms::conditional_effects(), so its values can differ slightly from 2.1.3.1 (#557).

Bug fixes

  • ecxll5 no longer fails to initialise when its starting value of f makes the powered denominator overflow. The curve is evaluated in a numerically stable, mathematically equivalent form. The default priors are unchanged. update() retains the formula stored in a saved fit; refit a previously saved ecxll5 object with bnec() to use this form (#600).

  • models() accepts every model group, including "decline" and "hormesis", and gives an informative error for input it cannot map (#170).

  • bnec() excludes, before fitting, an equation left with no group-level term on a grouping variable the formula names, and records why. 2.1.3.1 fitted it and then stopped after sampling with “Group-level variable(s) … not found in dataset” (#470).

  • bnec() drops a parameter an equation lacks from every (par | group) term that names it, not only the first (#470).

  • check_formula() refuses a missing grouping variable in any (par | group) term, not only the first (#466).

  • bnec() accepts a user prior on a group-level standard deviation or on ogl(), which the initial-value search of 2.1.3.1 refused (#245).

  • bnec() accepts a lognormal or constant() prior on a curve parameter, and sample_priors() draws from both (#84, #244, #302).

  • sample_priors() draws a bounded prior from the truncated distribution. 2.1.3.1 resampled the draws that fell inside the bounds with replacement, which repeated values under tight bounds.

  • sample_priors(plot = NA) returns the draws, as documented (#244).

  • A prior taken from a fitted object, whose bounds are stored as "", no longer stops the initial-value search (#141).

  • set.seed() before bnec() makes the fit repeatable, and seed = NA is accepted (#310).

  • bnec() clamps a bernoulli, binomial, beta_binomial or Beta response of exactly 0 or 1 inside the unit interval when it searches for initial values on the identity link, as it already did on the logit link (#162).

  • bnec() finds a model set or a predictor transformation defined in the calling function or chunk (#319).

  • bnec() fits an integer response with negative values as gaussian without a family argument (#272).

  • bnec() with family = "beta" fits a Beta model, and a string naming a function that is not a family is refused (#256).

  • bnec() refuses a binomial or beta_binomial formula without trials() once, naming the missing term (#442).

  • bnec() refuses a column name that is not syntactic, and names its make.names() form (#398).

  • bnec() no longer gives two warnings from min() when it builds the priors of a gaussian response with no positive value (#210, #229).

  • crf((log(x))) and crf(sqrt(log(x) + 1)) are read as written, and a predictor wrapped in I() compiles (#479).

  • update() keeps the fitted family when given new data, and treats a family equal to the fitted one as unchanged. 2.1.3.1 asked for force_fit = TRUE on such calls even where the family was unchanged. update() also fits the boundary-corrected response it checked (#256, #274, #435).

  • update() on a model set with one equation left returns a bayesnecfit (#288).

  • amend(add = ) works on a Gamma fit, excluding the equations Gamma cannot fit on the identity link (#436).

  • amend(add = ) samples an added equation with the set’s backend, algorithm and save_pars, and with a named list in priors gives each added equation its own element (#489).

  • A model set can combine equations with different numbers of posterior draws, where c() in 2.1.3.1 stopped with “subscript out of bounds”. The model average contains as many draws as the equation with the fewest, and each equation’s share is sampled from all of its draws (#548, #583).

  • compare_estimates() and compare_posterior() return the names of the fits unchanged in posterior_data. 2.1.3.1 turned a name that is not a syntactic R name, such as "2018", into "X2018", which then did not match prob_diff and diff_data.

  • autoplot() on a model set with multi_facet = FALSE honours plot = FALSE and restores the page prompt (#444).

  • plot() accepts position_legend as x and y coordinates, as documented (#278).

  • ggbnec_data() refuses an xform that is not a function on a model set, as it does on a single fit (#278).

  • check_priors() on a model set restores the page prompt and closes its PDF device on exit. It now returns named plots invisibly; check_priors() and check_chains() no longer print a model extraction message for each equation (#459).

  • extraDistr is listed in Suggests, since brms needs it to evaluate a beta_binomial likelihood.

  • autoplot(ecx = TRUE) no longer fails for a gaussian equation without bot.

Documentation and vignettes

  • example1, example2, example2b and example3 remain vignettes and are installed with the package. The other worked examples, including example4 and example5, which were vignettes in 2.1.3.1, are now articles on the package website (https://open-aims.github.io/bayesnec/articles/) and are not installed, so vignette("example4") and vignette("example5") no longer find them.

  • The article Hurdle and zero-inflated concentration-response models is new and fits nassarius with bnec_hurdle() and the two-block families (#175).

  • The article Modelling growth data and other potentially negative response values is new. It compares approaches on simulated growth data and then fits alga (#193).

  • The article Grouping and factor covariates is new. It fits lum31 with group-level terms, bnec_group() and bnec_joint() (#33).

  • The article A complete analysis workflow is new. It takes one lum31 zinc plate read at 15 minutes from data to estimates, fitting model = "all" with ogl(conc_group) and disp("power") (#219, #367).

  • The article Hormesis and the no-significant-effect concentration is new. It sets out the candidate no-effect estimates of a hormetic curve and fits the hormesis equations to published data, including the lettuce series of van Ewijk and Hoekstra (1993), which bayesnec now distributes as inst/extdata/hormesis_lettuce_1993.csv (#570, #573).

  • vignette("example3"), “Priors”, is rewritten. It covers the default priors, the choice between prior_type sets, fixing a parameter, and priors in models with group-level terms.

  • The article Comparisons and exceedance probabilities, formerly the vignette “Comparing posterior predictions”, is rewritten on published data. It compares the seven herbicides of herbicide, and the three climate scenarios of coral_colour and coral_pam, in place of simulated data, and uses exceedance() to compare the N(S)EC of each herbicide with a guideline value for diuron (#534).

  • example5 is rewritten as the article Installation and setup, and vignette("example1"), vignette("example2") and the README refer to it (#342).

  • vignette("example1") gains sections on the scale of the predictor, counts observed over an exposure, preparing the response, censoring and non-constant dispersion (#173, #181, #191, #193, #194).

  • vignette("example2") demonstrates screen_models() and fitting a model set in parallel (#184, #248).

  • vignette("example2b") and ?models state that NEC.3() and NEC.4() in the drc package correspond to nec3param and nec4param, and that NEC.2() has no counterpart (#139).

  • ?models states that a model group names a response shape, and which equations each family excludes (#170, #285).

  • ?autoplot states that a model set plotted with multi_facet = FALSE returns a list of plots (#459).

  • Vignette figures are PNG files, which render in the HTML vignettes (#178).

bayesnec 2.1.3.02024-08-19

  • Added citation for JSS manuscript describing bayesnec.

bayesnec 2.1.2.02024-03-28

  • Added step function to toolkit to allow for brms non-linear formula evaluation (89edef72).

bayesnec 2.1.1.02023-09-26

  • Fixed issues with summary and print methods (bf058f36).

  • Plotting methods now display the proper no-effect toxicity legend label (2be55d51).

  • Implemented native brms::beta_binomial() instead of custom family beta_binomial2 (c6c78fb7).

  • compare_* functions now have N(S)EC as default behaviour (c4c84ba1).

  • Changed argument name precision to resolution in many functions to maintain syntax compatibility with brms (727d6700).

  • Standardised plot style between sample_priors and check_priors (6c59af07).

bayesnec 2.1.0.32023-03-29

  • Improved speed in test runs for CRAN (d5d097fb).

  • Aligned generic method consistency for rhat (afb10577).

  • Fixed a bug relating to 01 bounded x data in define_prior (3ab93e0).

  • Fixed messages returned for set_distirbution (f483160).

  • Reduced n_trials and deleted unnecessary set.seed in while call for make_good_inits (3c5f084).

bayesnec 2.1.0.22023-02-20

  • Fixed bug introduced when implementing recycling the seed passed to bnec (01394a17).

  • Included additional criteria in the initial values algorithm to ensure initial values can be fit in stan (fe89484a).

bayesnec 2.1.0.12023-02-07

  • Cleaned parameter title names in sample_priors (6973bae1).

  • Small tweak to initialisation search, such that the seed used for a bnec call (via ... arguments to brms::brm) gets recycled and therefore it generates the same initialisation values across platforms (c74a3c46).

bayesnec 2.1.0.02022-12-15

  • Many improvements to package following suggestions from JSS editors. These include many things like dependency on R 4.1 to support native pipeOp, revamp of predict method for classes, major overhaul on package documentation, and much more. All issues were dealt with collectively via a milestone.

bayesnec 2.0.2.52022-10-31

  • Fixed issue with new “inits”–>“init” argument name in brm (30eb8e6).

bayesnec 2.0.2.42022-04-21

  • Fixed issue with new prior structures in brms (c5c16be).

bayesnec 2.0.2.32022-03-28

  • Fixed issue with expand_manec (1ced4d4).

  • Fixed issue with check_formula (87fab44).

bayesnec 2.0.2.2

  • Fixed issue with gsub substitution of x in original brms non-linear formulas, and added various tests (fa588fb).

bayesnec 2.0.2.1

  • Fixed vignette formula bugs (162fec9).

bayesnec 2.0.22021-10-17

  • Fixed CRAN bugs related to testthat (cfe9f20).

  • Changed decline detection behaviour in function check_data (c2744e3).

bayesnec 2.0.12021-09-20

  • Addition of herbicide data (2b13ef5).

  • streamlined check_* functions for negative predictors vectors – no error anymore (via check_data), now drop models with informative message (via check_models) (f134311).

bayesnec 2.02021-09-16

  • bnec now works exclusively with formulas (4bccc07, d3531b4, bccb0da, 340269e).

  • Added +, c and update methods via a common class bnecfit (d5e81ab, 3adf3fa).

  • Fixes to ecx, nec and nsec following new formula-based implementation (6ec1372, 0a9d307 and 19a37b9).

  • Fixes to predict methods following formula-based implementation (8843a1c, 08484a7).

  • Dispersion now takes a bayesnecfit as input (200bc11).

bayesnec 1.1.0

  • Added brms::bernoulli to the list of allowed model distributions (7606461).

  • Made identity the default link (6640867).

  • Added more controls and tweaks to checking model relative to input data (85a3819), 065a445).

  • Added formula and model.frame methods to main classes (9df4a64).

  • Upgraded ggbnec to autoplot as bayesnec standard ggplot2 plotting method (65fe15f).

  • Enhanced handling of argument loo_controls in bnec to allow argument for both brms::add_criterion and loo::loo_model_weights (9712fcc).

  • Added Bayesian R2 to summary (9a71a3c).

  • Expanded bnec’s capacity to accept input x and y vectors, data frames (f256b39) and formulas (32e74ac).

  • Corrected error for logit link cases for the beta_binomial2 where data contain 0 and 1 to ensure appropriate prior values on top and bot (4158237).

  • Series of internal fixes to standardise function class outputs (81369bb, 1c70efe, 5bce2b5, 455ca70, 5e6b41e).

bayesnec 1.0.12021-07-02

  • If link functions are not specified in bnec, then the default link function is used; previous versions of bayesnec used the identity link.

  • An additional family has been added beta_binomial2 for over-dispersed binomial data.

  • The package supports using link functions for generalised modelling, which appears to be more stable and is also in line with more typical generalised modelling approaches.

  • There are multiple options for model weights calculation from the loo package. The default is “pseudobma BB”.

  • There is now a compare_posterior function that also includes a bootstrapping procedure. This can be used to compare model fits across different datasets, or even different model sets for the same dataset (ie nec v ecx models). Please see the vignette for examples of usage.

  • There is a vignette detailing the models available in bayesnec. Note that not all models are suitable for all families, and also depending if link functions are used.

  • A new check_chains function has been added to allow chain plotting in base R and that works more smoothly with plotting chains for multiple fits for bayesmanec objects.
